subject: Attaching validate(need()) error messages directly to inputs

messages.author: b26ed5bf1a093922
messages.subject: Attaching validate(need()) error messages directly to inputs
parts:
Hey everyone,

I've written quite a large app and I'm now going through the process of cleaning things up and adding proper error messages using validate(need()). The really nice thing about writing error messages this way is that they propagate throughout the app, with any downstream objects or plots also displaying the same error.

I'm having a bit of an issue though, because I have some inputs which need to take particular values, or the app will produce errors (i.e. numeric inputs which can only take positive values). What's more, I call these inputs a hundred or so times throughout the app, and often dynamically - i.e. input[[paste0("number", i)]]. So if I have to write error messages every time a reactive object or output uses the input, I would end up writing similar chunks of code hundreds of times throughout the app - something like validate(need(input$number1 >= 1, "Error: the input must be positive". And things are even more complicated when I write the error messages for when the input is called dynamically. And of course this completey misses what's so nice about the validate(need()) system.

So what I'm wondering if is there's any way to attach or associate a validate() style warning message directly with an input? This way, I would only have to write the error message once, and it would propagate throughout the app every time the input is called.

The closest I can think of getting to this would be to set up all the inputs like this:
ui.R:
numericInput("number1", "Enter number 1:")

server.R:
number1 <- reactive({
x <- input$number1
validate(need(x >= 1, "Error: the input must be positive))
return(x)
})

And then in the rest of the server, you can just call number1() instead of input$number1 to get the error message.

But I just thought I'd check if there is a better way of doing this. Especially since, as I mentioned, I often call these inputs dynamically, so implementing this throughout the app is not simply a case of "find all and replace".

Cheers,
John
